newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX ends at 6th successive closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX ends at 6th successive closing high.

text.p: Hungary's BUX share index hit its seventh successive closing high on Monday mainly supported by good macroeconomic figures announced on Friday, traders and analysts said.
On Monday the BUX closed at a preliminary 6,362.93 points, up 43.92 points or 0.7 percent.
"People who are investing internationally and in emerging markets are very well aware of Hungary's track record," said Roger Monson of Daiwa Europe Ltd.
"I think that we look forward to some good support for the market".

On Friday the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) cut four of its five repo rates by 50 basis points each. Later on Friday the NBH announced a March trade surplus of $46 million and a current account surplus of $19 million.
"The repo rate cuts and...trade figures supported today's rise," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust.
He added that although last week the closing BUX rose each day, minimal gains on two consecutive days almost amounted to corrections.
"On Wednesday and Thursday the BUX fell some 70 to 80 points and only recovered afterwards," Revesz said.
Pharmaceuticals Egis put on 290 forints to end at 11,990 and Richter gained 185 forints closing at 15,890.
Revesz said investors continued to move their funds from the Czech Republic to Hungary.
Monson added that the Hungarian market's long-term outlook remained good and investors' interest in Hungarian papers was not fading.
"The quality of earnings and the outlook for an improved economic trend..all make people willing to keep playing," Monson said.
